title: One-Dribble Closeout Attack
description: The receiver catches a pass as a defender closes out and must beat the closeout with one hard dribble into a pull-up, floater or lay-up.

content.objective: Read the closeout and attack it with one efficient dribble, using the defender's momentum against them.
content.setup: Passer at the top of the key; offense at the wing; defense starts under the basket.
content.organization: Rotate passer to offense to defense to passer.
instructions: The defender passes to the wing and closes out hard.
The receiver catches in triple threat and reads the closeout.
If the defender flies past the shot fake, attack with one dribble into a pull-up.
If the defender closes high, drive the high foot with one dribble to the rim.
Play live for three seconds after the catch.
coachingPoints: Catch ready: feet set, eyes on the rim.
One dribble only: long and low.
commonMistakes: Holding the ball and letting the defender recover.
Two or three dribbles that let the help come.
content.safety: Defenders close out under control, chopping their feet; no running through the shooter.
progressions: Add a help defender who rotates on the drive.
Kick out to a corner shooter if help arrives.
regressions: Defender closes out at half speed and shows a lean.
No live play after the decision.
variations: Allow a jab-step before the dribble.
successCriteria: Scores or creates a clean shot on 6 of 10 possessions.
content.gameApplication: Attacking closeouts is the second half of every drive-and-kick; one dribble keeps help defenders out of the play.
